pullRequest.title: feat: establish Document Trail product baseline

criterion.text: Baseline branch is pushed and represented by a draft PR.

criteria.summary: The Document Trail baseline is represented by PR #435 from the pushed agent/document-trail branch.
evidence: GitHub reports PR #435 at exact head 5c70027cbd4ebff3bcea57e73b1f356ae972dae5.
The PR is linked to Issue #434 through its closing reference.
criteria.reportedValidation: The read-only GitHub observation found the expected branch, PR number, linked issue, and exact head revision.
criteria.reviewQuestion: Does this pull request give the baseline a clear, reviewable delivery home?

criterion.text: Both Document Trail Nx projects build, typecheck, and test successfully.

criteria.summary: The reusable domain package and local application define focused Nx build, typecheck, and test targets.
evidence: The PR records a focused Nx run for both projects with build, test, and typecheck targets.
The PR records 37 focused tests passing; this is a declared result to verify during review, not a compiler-generated claim.
criteria.reportedValidation: PR #435 reports focused Nx build, test, and typecheck success for both baseline projects; the Guided Code Review branch independently reruns the affected projects.
openGaps: The human reviewer must decide whether the reported proof is sufficient for baseline acceptance.
criteria.reviewQuestion: Do the focused project contracts and recorded validation adequately prove both Document Trail projects?

criterion.text: Current architecture and Factory review kits load as prepared trails.

criteria.summary: Prepared-trail manifests connect the Mission Rail architecture and Factory learning documents to curated checkpoint sets.
evidence: The prepared manifests name their source documents and checkpoint JSON.
The local server exposes prepared trails through /trails/<slug>.
criteria.reportedValidation: The local prepared-trail loader and checkpoint validator pass for the generated manifests and checkpoint sets.
openGaps: Visual behavior remains a human QA observation rather than a compiler claim.
criteria.reviewQuestion: Can a reviewer open both prepared learning trails without manually locating source and checkpoint files?

criterion.text: The PR explains known prototype limitations and identifies the next small product slices.

criteria.summary: The PR body describes the baseline, validation, exclusions, and the policy that later product changes move through smaller issue-bound pull requests.
evidence: The PR body identifies the baseline contents and explicit exclusions.
Issue #434 and the PR delivery note identify future work as small product slices rather than additions to the baseline.
criteria.reportedValidation: README and QA checklist paths are present in the observed PR diff; prose quality remains a human review decision.
openGaps: The reviewer may request clearer limitations or next-slice wording.
criteria.reviewQuestion: Does the PR make the prototype boundary and next delivery shape understandable enough to accept as a baseline?

criterion.text: Future product work does not accumulate directly on the baseline branch after review begins.

criteria.summary: New Document Trail work has moved to issue-bound stacked branches instead of accumulating on the baseline branch.
evidence: Invoice Inspect is tracked by Issue #436 and stacked PR #437 rather than appended to PR #435.
Guided Code Review is tracked by Issue #438 and this branch is based on the baseline branch.
criteria.reportedValidation: GitHub shows follow-on work in separate issue-bound branches and PRs.
criteria.reviewQuestion: Does the observed follow-on work demonstrate that the baseline branch has stopped accumulating unrelated product slices?
